_comment: Narration script for the audio guide. This is the single source of truth:
the app reads it to know what to say, and worker/gen-voice.mjs reads it to
generate the recorded MP3s. Edit the text here, re-run the generator, and
Written to be heard, not read. It is deliberately not identical to the
on-screen copy: numerals are spelled the way a person says them ('two
percent', not '2%') because text-to-speech mangles symbols, and the
sentences are shorter than the prose.
Ids are stable filenames. Renaming one orphans its MP3.

beats.text: One family bought decades ago. Their neighbor bought last year. For nearly identical houses, the newer owner can owe ten times more property tax. This is a map of that gap across every parcel in San Francisco.
Type your address, and the map will take you there. The rest of this story reads differently when it is your own block on the screen.
Since 1978, California taxes a home on its purchase price, rising at most two percent a year, until it sells again. Prices have far outrun two percent, so the longer you hold, the wider the gap.
Each block here is a neighborhood. Taller and darker means a bigger gap. The Sunset, the Richmond, and West of Twin Peaks tower over the rest.
Fifteen years ago the market sat closer to what people were taxed on. As values climbed and owners stayed put, the yearly savings grew with them.
This house changed hands in 2011 without a reassessment. It is still taxed on 29 percent of what it is worth, about 65 thousand dollars a year less than a new buyer would owe.
The map is yours from here. Search an address, tap any parcel, or turn on Compare to line up your block against a neighbor's.
Audio guide on. I will read each parcel as you open it.
